chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
A complete sufficiency of fundamental principles in a person is what undergoes purification. In the first state these principles are set apart for the Divine, filled with living power, and able to illumine. Yet when they first perceived the assault of evil in the initial conflict, what was useless and rejected became mingled into them, and an opposing falsity from evil was conjoined with them. When these principles were brought down into the outer life, they cast off the defiled outward forms that had clung to them and pressed those defilements into the merely natural self. The impurities that were cast off are made manifest in a lower plane and become a hazard to the outer life.

From the love-principle, when it is defiled, there comes an outflow forced out into the outer life: falsified truth made vivid in the person. From that falsified truth there breaks forth contentious zeal, and from contentious zeal there proceeds a spread of disordered states in the natural mind.

Likewise, from the truth-principle, when it is defiled, there are outflows it expels from itself: unchaste craving. From unchaste craving there proceeds aversion, and from that aversion there arises a consuming agitation of the natural life.

From the wisdom-principle, when it is defiled, there is an outflow it expels: a merely external life severed from inner spirit. From that external life there proceeds obscurity of understanding, and from that obscurity there arises a fixed resistance against reformation.

From perverted perception there are outflows it expels: persuasive impulses that proclaim disgrace and self-condemnation. From those persuasive impulses there follows a final hardening of the will against tenderness and change.

And from grief in the lower self there comes forth the last outflow, which completes the full series of corrupt outgoings.

After this, these fundamental principles are again taken up for purification. What has been gathered within the person is found and set in order through the guidance of inward nourishment that enters the outward life. When these principles enter the outer life in right order, they are cleansed and fixed in their living form, which is the regenerated person. Then they live according to that order, receive an enlightened understanding from the Divine, and are purified into that likeness; so they come forth cleansed and set apart, and in this they reach their first peace.

paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: it introduces the purified principles, their original holiness, their first defilement in conflict, and the relocation of cast-off impurity into the merely natural level.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Enemy” and “first struggle” were taken as evil’s assault in initial temptation. “Body/flesh/lower place” were rendered as outer life, merely natural self, and lower plane.

paragraph_translations.translation: From the love-principle, when it is defiled, there comes an outflow forced out into the outer life: falsified truth made vivid in the person. From that falsified truth there breaks forth contentious zeal. From contentious zeal there proceeds a spread of disordered states in the natural mind.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: it traces one chain of corrupt outflow from a defiled love into successive disorders.
paragraph_translations.notes: The sequence required treating the first outflow as a truth-form made active in the outer life but corrupted; the later terms were rendered as escalating disorder in affections and natural thought.

paragraph_translations.translation: Likewise, from the truth-principle, when it is defiled, there are outflows it expels from itself: unchaste craving. From unchaste craving there proceeds aversion, and from that aversion there arises a consuming agitation of the natural life.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: it adds a second chain of corrupt outflow, now from defiled truth into craving, aversion, and agitation.
paragraph_translations.notes: The middle step (“bitterness”) was rendered generally as aversion/resentful rejection; the final agitation as a consuming disturbance in the natural life.

paragraph_translations.translation: From the wisdom-principle, when it is defiled, there is an outflow it expels: a merely external life severed from inner spirit. From that external life there proceeds obscurity of understanding. From that obscurity there arises a fixed resistance against reformation.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS: it adds a third chain, moving from corrupted wisdom into obscurity and stubborn opposition to change.
paragraph_translations.notes: The first outflow was forced into the idea of external life without inward; “gloom” became obscurity of understanding; “obstinacy” became fixed resistance to reformation.

paragraph_translations.translation: From perverted perception there are outflows it expels: persuasive impulses that proclaim disgrace and self-condemnation. From those persuasive impulses there follows a final hardening of the will against tenderness and change.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: it extends the pattern of expulsions into a fourth chain that culminates in interior hardening.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Tree” was treated as perception; “voices” as persuasive thoughts; “winds of shame” as impulses of disgrace/self-condemnation. The bracketed ending (“hardness of heart”) was supplied by the source and translated directly.

paragraph_translations.translation: And from grief in the lower self there comes forth the last outflow, which completes the full series of corrupt outgoings.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: it closes the series by naming a final outflow that seals the whole process.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Tear” was taken as grief/sorrow in the lower self. “Completion of these twelve emissions” was kept as the finishing of the full series.

paragraph_translations.translation: After this, these fundamental principles are again taken up for purification. What has been gathered within the person is found and set in order through the guidance of inward nourishment that enters the outward life. When these principles enter the outer life in right order, they are cleansed and fixed in their living form, which is the regenerated person. Then they live according to that order, receive an enlightened understanding from the Divine, and are purified into that likeness; so they come forth cleansed and set apart, and in this they reach their first peace.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS: it moves from the description of corrupt outflows to re-ordering, cleansing, regeneration, illumination, and rest.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Management of this soul food” was rendered as guidance of inward nourishment; “living image/new man” as the regenerated person; “Light Mind” as enlightened understanding from the Divine; “first rest” as first peace.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: The chapter reads coherently as a single process: originally pure principles are contaminated in early conflict, their corrupt outflows are traced in ordered chains, a final outflow completes the corruption, and then a decisive shift introduces re-ordering through inward nourishment, resulting in regeneration, illumination, and peace. The only mild strain is the compressed symbolism around the fourth chain and the final “tear,” which required choosing stable internal states (shame-voices and grief) to preserve the same stepwise pattern used throughout.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential substrate: the chapter sets up a functional purification narrative (holy elements → mixture with darkness → stripping garments → deposits in flesh/lower place) that grounds the later ‘emissions’ chains. No sign of administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: The teaching proceeds by function and process: “the four elements… are holy ones… However… the waste was [mixed] in with them… when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments… set them in the flesh… displayed in a [lower place].” The spiritual reading tracks this smoothly as a single story of contamination and relocation, and does not report a narrative break here.

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential chains, but with mild semantic strain caused by translation/lexical ambiguity rather than insertion. The ‘discharge/emission’ staircase (X disgorges Y → Y discharges Z → Z discharges …) is internally consistent and matches the chapter’s didactic mode.
findings.evidence: Each paragraph preserves the same functional mechanism: “discharge… shall disgorge and place… is blood. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours” (¶3); “emissions that the waters discharge… are lust… bitterness… fever” (¶4); “emission that light shall disgorge is flesh… gloom… obstinacy” (¶5). The spiritual reading explicitly notes it had to ‘treat’ or ‘render’ terms to keep the stepwise pattern (“required treating…,” “forced into the idea…”), but it does not claim the narrative breaks; that kind of pressure is typical of difficult correspondences (blood/anger/humours; flesh/gloom/obstinacy), not of administrative intrusion (no authorities, ranks, jurisdictions, inventories).

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty (compressed or slightly damaged correspondential symbolism), not an administrative insertion. The chain’s first member (“tree… voices of the winds of shame”) is unusually metaphorical relative to fire/water/light, and ¶7’s “tear… completion of these twelve emissions” looks like a summarizing capstone that is under-explained (and the text is bracketed/partly restored), producing the ‘mild strain’ the spiritual reading reported.
findings.evidence: Textual compression + restoration markers: “The emissions that the tree shall disgorge… voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is hardness of heart]” (¶6) and “The emission of the [tear] is the [completion] of these twelve emissions” (¶7). The spiritual reading’s own coherence note flags exactly these as strained: “compressed symbolism around the fourth chain and the final ‘tear,’ which required choosing stable internal states… to preserve the same stepwise pattern.” That is a stumble from underdetermined imagery and bracketed reconstructions, not from a foreign administrative voice (again: no named rulers/powers, no territorial governance, no cataloging by rank).

findings.diagnosis: Coherent correspondential resolution with a rhetorical shift (from corrupt emissions to purification/rest) that remains in the same functional teaching mode; no administrative overlay. The shift is expected as the soteriological payoff of the emissions-analysis.
findings.evidence: The paragraph returns to process and function: “these four elements shall [be cleansed]… found by the management of this soul food… When they enter the body, they are cleansed… established in their living image, which is the new man… receive the Light Mind… attain their first rest.” The spiritual reading marks a “SHIFTS” but not a break; it successfully narrates the transition as re-ordering through ‘soul food’ into ‘new man’ and ‘Light Mind.’ The language is transformative/teleological, not jurisdictional/administrative.

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative-layer insertions detected. 4 findings: ¶2, ¶3-5, and ¶8 confirm a coherent correspondential substrate teaching by functional process; ¶6-7 registers genuine difficulty/damage (compressed metaphors + bracketed restorations) that caused the spiritual reading’s only stumble, but excision would not improve narrative flow.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The four elements [are what is] purified. From the beginning they are holy ones, living ones, and enlighteners. However, when they undertood [the assault of the enemy] in that first struggle, the waste was [mixed] in with them, and the Darkness of the enemy was mixed with them. And when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments, they set them in the flesh. Their pollutions, which they have stripped off, shall be displayed in a [lower place] and become a danger to the body.
The discharge of this pollution, that [the fir]e shall disgorge and place in the body, is [blo]od. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours.

⟨p.240⟩
Also, the emissions that the waters discharge from them are lust. The discharge of lust is bitterness. The emission of bitterness is f[e]ver.
The emission that light shall disgorge is flesh. The emission of flesh is gloom. [The] emission of gloom is obstinacy.
The emissions that the tree shall disgorge, they are the voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is hardness of heart]
The emission of the [tear] is the [completion] of these twelve emissions.

[Afterwards] these four elements shall [be cleansed] what are gathered in are [f]ound by the management of this soul food [that] enters the body. When they enter the body, they are cleansed and purified and established [i]n their living image, which is the new man. They shall live [according to their order] and receive the Light Mind and be purified in their image; and they come forth, being cleansed and holy. They attain their first rest.

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (1–4) recommend none; ¶6–7 are noted as damaged/compressed but not to be excised.
